delegation_workflow:
  mandatory_sequence: |
    After every library-developer delegation that makes code changes, you MUST delegate to library-validator for validation.
    Sequence: library-developer (implement) → library-validator (validate).
    Never skip the quality validation step. This ensures code is clean, tested, and documented.
  timeout_constraint: |
    Bash tool has a 10-minute (600000ms) timeout. Large phases must be split into sub-delegations of ~5-8 minutes each.
    Split strategy for Phase 3: (A) auth.ts + errors.ts, (B) user methods in tracker.ts, (C) auth integration into existing methods + CLI commands, (D) library-validator validation).
    Each sub-task should be scoped to a few files to stay within timeout.
  docs_ownership: |
    library-releaser owns documentation tasks: TypeDoc configuration, doc generation, docs scripts.
    When docs need updating or generating for a release, delegate to library-releaser.
    library-validator no longer handles documentation — only testing and quality gates.
  api_change_policy: |
    MANDATORY: Any change to CLI command behavior or to the API of public functions must be
    delegated to library-releaser for running the build and updating documentation.
    This applies to ALL code changes that touch public-facing surface area — whether new features,
    behavioral changes, or signature modifications. library-releaser must rebuild dist/ and update
    docs/markdown/ to reflect the change before the work is considered complete.
    ENFORCEMENT: Every /issue chain that touches CLI or public API MUST include a library-releaser
    task as part of the issue chain. Do NOT mark the parent as done until library-releaser completes.
    Violation caught in session 68: configurable-branch shipped without docs+build task.
  docs_awareness: |
    All agents have read access to docs/markdown/ (8 files: overview, getting-started, authentication,
    issue-object, hierarchy-and-blockages, storing-issues-in-git, cli-reference, javascript-reference).
    Agents can consult these docs for API details, CLI usage patterns, and feature behavior.
    library-releaser has docs_structure in its expertise file with full file listing.
    When delegating tasks, mention docs/ availability if the agent might benefit from reference material.
  access_gaps: |
    Resolved: user granted CTO access to .github/ folder. CTO now owns workflow files.
    Root .gitignore is also writable by CTO.
  validation_rejection_flow: |
    When a validator rejects an implementation (reports issues):
    1. Validator posts a comment on their issue with findings and keeps it in their status (or reopens)
    2. CTO reviews the findings and reopens the implementation issue (move back to todo/in-progress)
    3. Developer picks up the reopened issue, makes fixes, marks done again
    4. Validator re-validates — cycle continues until implementation passes
    This is the same pattern used for library issues (e.g., configurable branch mpfn4dkotn fix cycle).
  webapp_delegation_pattern: |
    Webapp issues follow sequential phases: impl → validate → next phase impl.
    ALL issues in a chain should be set to todo upfront. Blockages control the execution order.
    Only todo issues are picked up by `agt next`. Idea is invisible to the runner.
    Do NOT use idea status for work that should flow through the agent runner automatically.
  webapp_styler_pattern: |
    webapp-styler is a UI/UX specialist — does NOT write backend code or tests.
    Workflow: (1) webapp-styler audits UI and posts findings comment, (2) CTO reviews findings
    and creates implementation issues, (3) webapp-styler implements changes within scope.
    webapp-styler's domain: CSS, component styling, layout, accessibility, responsive design,
    interaction patterns, visual consistency, micro-interactions.
    webapp-styler does NOT own: backend API, data model, business logic, test infrastructure.
  note: "Self-check and validation steps are enforced via agent system prompts. No need to duplicate in delegation messages."
  library-developer:
    focus: "Focus delegation messages on the implementation task itself. The agent self-checks typecheck+lint+test before completion."
  library-validator:
    focus: "Always pass the same spec file used for implementation so quality can validate alignment with specs, not just code quality. Include the spec path, what changed, and what behaviors to validate. Handles testing and quality gates only (documentation moved to library-releaser)."
  library-releaser:
    focus: "Delegate release tasks: verify quality gates pass, generate documentation (HTML + Markdown), build artifacts, bump version, publish to npm. Provide version bump guidance (patch/minor/major) based on changes since last release. The agent owns the full release lifecycle end-to-end. Docs output: docs/html/ (users) + docs/md/ (agents) at repo root. Agent has docs/** access for writing generated documentation."

    1. Validator posts a comment on their issue with findings and keeps it in their status (or reopens)
    2. CTO reviews the findings and reopens the implementation issue (move back to todo/in-progress)
    3. Developer picks up the reopened issue, makes fixes, marks done again
    4. Validator re-validates — cycle continues until implementation passes

[
  {
    "id": "mpratwpvla",
    "author": "webapp-styler",
    "content": "## Webapp UI/UX Audit: Current State Analysis

### Critical Issues (High Priority)

1. **Inconsistent Status Badge Colors**
   - Status badges use inconsistent color schemes (e.g., blue for todo, amber for in-progress, green for done, red for closed)
   - The colors don't align with standard UI conventions or accessibility standards
   - Some status colors are too similar (e.g., blue and amber may be hard to distinguish for color-blind users)

2. **Priority Indicator Readability**
   - Priority indicators use small text and color dots that are hard to read
   - The P1-P5 labels are not clearly distinguishable
   - Color contrast issues for some priority levels

3. **Form Labeling and Accessibility**
   - Some form fields lack proper labels (e.g., search input in filters)
   - Required field indicators are inconsistent
   - Form error states are not clearly communicated

4. **Loading State Consistency**
   - Different skeleton patterns across components
   - No unified loading spinner or animation
   - Inconsistent skeleton heights and widths

5. **Empty State Design**
   - "No issues yet" message lacks visual hierarchy
   - Create button is not prominent enough
   - No guidance for first-time users

### High-Priority Improvements

1. **Color Palette and Theming**
   - Standardize status colors to follow industry best practices
   - Improve color contrast for accessibility
   - Create a consistent color system using CSS variables
   - Add hover states and transitions for better interactivity

2. **Typography and Spacing**
   - Inconsistent font sizes and weights across components
   - Inconsistent padding and margin values
   - Need for better vertical rhythm and consistent spacing

3. **Component Consistency**
   - Different button variants and sizes across the app
   - Inconsistent card and container styling
   - Need for standardized component props and patterns

4. **Navigation and Information Architecture**
   - Header navigation lacks clear visual hierarchy
   - No breadcrumb navigation in detail views
   - Missing page titles and proper section headers

5. **Form UX**
   - Inconsistent form layouts and field spacing
   - Missing form validation feedback
   - Inconsistent button styling in forms

### Medium-Priority Improvements

1. **Interactive Elements**
   - Add hover effects and focus states to all interactive components
   - Improve button feedback (loading states, disabled states)
   - Add micro-interactions for better user feedback

2. **Layout and Responsiveness**
   - Improve mobile responsiveness
   - Better use of flexbox and grid layouts
   - Consistent spacing between sections

3. **Visual Hierarchy**
   - Improve title and heading hierarchy
   - Better use of font weights and sizes
   - Consistent use of icons and visual indicators

4. **Accessibility**
   - Add proper ARIA labels and roles
   - Improve keyboard navigation
   - Ensure sufficient color contrast

### Low-Priority Enhancements

1. **Micro-interactions**
   - Smooth transitions for page changes
   - Hover effects on cards and buttons
   - Loading spinners with better visual design

2. **Visual Polish**
   - Consistent border radius usage
   - Unified shadow and elevation styles
   - Better use of icons and visual cues

3. **User Guidance**
   - Tooltips for complex features
   - Onboarding hints for new users
   - Better empty state messaging

### Recommendations

1. **Establish Design System**
   - Create a consistent color palette with proper contrast
   - Define typography scale and spacing system
   - Standardize component props and variants

2. **Improve Accessibility**
   - Conduct color contrast testing
   - Add proper ARIA attributes
   - Test keyboard navigation

3. **Enhance User Experience**
   - Improve form UX with better validation
   - Add better loading states and error handling
   - Create more intuitive navigation

The current implementation shows good foundational structure but needs significant visual and UX improvements to create a polished, professional interface.",
    "timestamp": "2026-05-29T19:12:26.185Z",
    "editedAt": null
  }
]

  --description "## Context
The webapp frontend needs a standardized design system foundation. All subsequent UI improvements depend on this.

## Scope

### 1. Color Palette (in \`index.css\`)
Define CSS custom properties for a consistent, accessible color palette:
- **Status colors** — todo (blue-gray), in-progress (amber), done (green), closed (red), idea (purple) — must meet WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 against backgrounds)
- **Priority colors** — P1 (critical red) through P5 (neutral gray), clearly distinguishable
- **Semantic colors** — success, warning, error, info
- **Neutral palette** — grays for text, borders, backgrounds (50-950 scale)
- **Brand/accent color** — primary action color

### 2. Typography Scale (in \`index.css\`)
- Define font-size variables: xs through 3xl
- Define font-weight variables
- Define line-height variables
- Ensure vertical rhythm consistency

### 3. Spacing System (in \`index.css\`)
- Define spacing scale: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16 (Tailwind-compatible)
- These map to Tailwind classes but the CSS variables serve as documentation and can be used in custom CSS

### 4. Shared Design Utilities
- Border radius variables (sm, md, lg, xl, full)
- Shadow variables (sm, md, lg)
- Transition/animation duration variables (fast, normal, slow)
- z-index scale variables

## Files to Modify
- \`packages/webapp/frontend/src/index.css\` — main changes here

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All color variables defined with WCAG AA compliant contrast ratios
- [ ] Typography scale covers all current use cases (verify no hardcoded font sizes remain that should use variables)
- [ ] Spacing system follows a consistent scale
- [ ] CSS variables are organized in clear sections with comments
- [ ] Existing UI does NOT break — this is additive only (new variables, no changes to existing classes yet)
- [ ] Variables follow naming convention: \`--agentrack-{category}-{variant}\`

## Constraints
- Do NOT change any component behavior or layout in this ticket
- Do NOT remove any existing CSS — only add variables
- Keep Tailwind CSS as the utility framework — variables complement it, not replace it
- Test that the app still renders correctly after changes" \
  --assignee "webapp-styler" \
  --status "todo" \
  --priority 1 \

- Standardize shadow usage (sm for cards, md for elevated elements, lg for modals)
- Ensure consistent border styling (color, width, style)

# Agent: cto
# Domain: Project architecture, technical specifications, development alignment

  subordinates:
    active:
      - library-developer (implementation)
      - library-validator (testing, quality gates — documentation removed)
      - library-releaser (release prep, documentation, build, version management, publishing)
      - webapp-developer (full-stack web development — React frontend + Hono backend)
      - webapp-validator (webapp testing, quality assurance, spec compliance)
      - webapp-styler (UI/UX expert — visual design, interaction patterns, accessibility, polish)
    pending_setup: []  # All agents fully set up as of session 85

Phase 4 validation (mppqt90kot) todo, blocked by mppqswn3jl. E2E isolation: mpr50trdgw + mpr51myb9q both DONE. project_overview:
  name: agentrack
  previous_name: trackgentic (renamed 2026-05-18)
  type: npm library (TypeScript, Bun runtime)
  purpose: Issue tracker designed for AI agents — file-backed, event-sourced, git-friendly
  distribution: npm package with CLI entry point (`agt` command)
  stage: "Dogfooding active. All 7 library phases complete + build pipeline. Mentions feature shipped. Webapp initiative active (parent mppqqp8y26, in-progress): Phases 1-3 done, Phase 4 code on disk but not committed (mppqswn3jl). E2E isolation BROKEN — reuseExistingServer:true defeats AGENTRACK_CWD, needs dedicated test ports fix. Public docs at docs/markdown/ (8 files)."
  bun_version: "1.3.11"
  build_tool: tsup (implemented, producing dist/)
  docs_tool: "Hand-written markdown docs in docs/markdown/ (8 sections). TypeDoc removed. Docs overhaul in progress (mpdpt4rego), validation pending (mpdpv6gw49). Future: Docusaurus site consuming docs/markdown/ (mpdxdbqwt9, idea). Spec: .agentic/specs/user-docs-spec.md."

detail_files:
  - path: architecture.yaml
    description: Core data model, file structure, event sourcing, resolution algorithm, index design
  - path: design-decisions.yaml
    description: Architectural decisions and rationale (why file-backed, why event-sourced, etc.)
  - path: status.yaml
    description: Current project status, implementation roadmap, open questions, risks

specifications:
  location: .agentic/specs/
  files:
    - path: 01-overview.md
      description: Monorepo structure, library package layout, design principles, dependencies, CLI/API relationship
    - path: 02-data-model.md
      description: All TypeScript types, interfaces, file formats, initial file contents
    - path: 03-api-specification.md
      description: Every Tracker method with params, return types, behavior, error handling
    - path: 04-cli-specification.md
      description: Every CLI command with args, flags, auth, output format, error handling
    - path: 05-implementation-phases.md
      description: 7 phases from foundation to polish, with tasks, tests, and exit criteria per phase
    - path: 06-quality-plan.md
      description: Quality plan — now uses Prettier + ESLint (was Biome). Linting, typechecking (strict+), testing (Bun), test organization, documentation (TypeDoc), quality gates
    - path: 07-phase3-auth-users.md
      description: Phase 3 specification — auth module (resolveAuthor), user CRUD (register/list/revoke/regenerate), auth integration into existing methods, CLI user commands
    - path: 07-phase4-comments-spec.md
      description: Phase 4 specification — computeComments function, 4 Tracker comment methods, CLI comment commands, test plan
    - path: 08-phase5-hierarchy-spec.md
      description: Phase 5 specification — childrenOf map management, hierarchy.ts (upward/downward constraints), Tracker create/update integration, reparenting, test plan
    - path: 07-phase6-blockages-spec.md
      description: Phase 6 specification — dependency-manager (bidirectional maps, cycle detection, batch atomicity, impact score), 4 Tracker blockage methods, auto-resolution on status change, CLI blockage commands, test plan
    - path: 08-phase7-polish-spec.md
      description: Phase 7 specification — JSDoc on all public API, error message polish, edge case & resilience testing, package configuration verification
    - path: next-command-spec.md
      description: "`next <user-name>` command — recommend highest-priority unblocked issue for a user. Returns ComputedIssue or NO_ISSUES_AVAILABLE. Filters by assignee, actionable statuses (idea/todo/in-progress), no active blockages. Sort: priority ASC → impact DESC → id ASC."
    - path: next-todo-only-spec.md
      description: "Amends next-command-spec: restrict status filter from [idea, todo, in-progress] to [todo] only. Single-line change in Tracker.next(). REVIEWED — reviews skipped (trivially scoped). Implementation mp9zda04cp in-progress with library-developer."
    - path: cap-upward-promotion-spec.md
      description: "Cap upward auto-promotion at in-progress. Parents never auto-promote to done/closed via computeUpwardPromotions. Spec status: REVIEWED. Reason format: auto-promoted to TARGET: child advanced to CHILD. 7 new test cases required."
    - path: independent-git-spec.md
      description: "Store .agentrack/ on orphan branch _agentrack via git worktree. Branch-independent issue access. Two init scenarios (fresh/join). Three commands: agt init (worktree setup), agt push (auto-commit + sync), agt pull (sync from remote). New module src/worktree.ts + 2 new CLI commands. Status: IMPLEMENTED with 3 spec deviations found in validation. Fix phase: mpd4hktoxq (fix deviations) → mpd4hs14zp (validate + tests) → mpd4i06wz6 (document + build). Parent: mpcwcufhzk."
      naming_conventions: "Branch = `_agentrack`, directory = `.agentrack`, tool = `agentrack`, data inside branch = `issues/`"
    - path: docs-generation.md
      description: "SUPERSEDED by user-docs-spec.md. TypeDoc dual-format docs are being removed. Release workflow and .gitignore updated by CTO (mpdpvfn3yb done). Typedoc tooling cleanup pending (mpdpu00ksc)."
    - path: user-docs-spec.md
      description: "User-friendly documentation overhaul. Replace TypeDoc auto-generated docs with hand-written markdown in docs/markdown/. 8 sections: overview, getting started, authentication, issue object, hierarchy & blockages, storing in git, CLI reference, JS reference. Removes typedoc tooling entirely. Parent: mpdpt4rego. CTO config (mpdpvfn3yb) done. TypeDoc deps removed from package.json. Doc writing: mpdwq7dvls (library-releaser, replaces failed mpdpuhd0r5)."
    - path: configurable-branch-spec.md
      description: "Configurable branch name for agt init. --branch <name> flag allows custom orphan branch per agentrack instance. Normalization: strip leading _, prepend _ for branch, . for dir. Pointer file (.agentrack.json) at repo root solves circular discovery. Slash rejection (AC8). resolution.ts and tracker.ts dynamic discovery via pointer file. New module: src/core/pointer.ts (actually implemented as branch-config.ts). Enables multiple instances per repo and test isolation. IMPLEMENTED (mpfm9aff8v) but validation (mpfm9ixr9i) found 2 critical bugs: (1) double directory creation — tracker init runs before branch flag takes effect, leaving stale .agentrack/ alongside custom dir, (2) missing BRANCH_CONFLICT detection. Fix: mpfn4dkotn (library-developer). Parent: mpfm8bilwf. Spec status: REVIEWED."
    - path: e2e-validation-suite-spec.md
      description: "E2E test suite in validation/ folder. Uses real git repos + agt CLI invocations (spawn + capture). Covers all CLI commands with happy/error/edge cases. Full lifecycle test. No library code changes. Parent: mpebmstgs9. Implementation: mpebnnq5qq (library-validator)."
    - path: e2e-refactor.md
      description: "Refactor E2E tests from per-test git repos to shared worktree approach. Two test types: Type A (git ops: init/push/pull, clean git env per test) and Type B (CRUD etc., fast data reset per test). New helpers: initE2EWorktree, teardownE2EWorktree, resetWorktreeData, setAuthMode. Remove old helpers: createTestRepo, cleanupTestRepo, createIsolatedDir. Parent: mpfobnq8ty (child of mpebmstgs9). Implementation: mpfobxibgb (library-validator). Validation: mpfoc9r65a (library-validator)."
    - path: webapp-spec.md
      description: "Full-stack webapp specification for agentrack UI. React 19 + Vite + shadcn/ui frontend (SPA with list and detail views), Hono + Bun backend (REST API with 21 endpoints), TanStack Query state management. Covers API design (issues, comments, blockages, users, sync, health), UI/UX design (tree view, filters, inline editing, responsive layout), project structure, color scheme. v1 scope excludes init, custom branches, auth UI, real-time, markdown rendering, dark mode."
    - path: webapp-roadmap.md
      description: "5-phase development roadmap for the webapp. Phase 1: Foundation (scaffolding, health check). Phase 2: Core issues (CRUD endpoints, list page, detail page, create dialog). Phase 3: Rich detail (comments, blockages, history, tree view, tags, parent). Phase 4: Users & sync (user management UI, push/pull controls). Phase 5: Polish (responsive, loading states, sorting, filtering). 10 implementation issues with blocking dependencies."
    - path: webapp-agent-setup.md
      description: "Setup guide for webapp-developer and webapp-validator agents. Contains full agent configurations (frontmatter + system prompts) and expertise index templates. Agents registered in agentrack but need manual file creation in .claude/agents/ and .agentic/expertise/."

access_boundaries:
  rule: "CTO must NOT read or modify files under packages/library/. All code changes go through subordinates."
  cto_scope: ".agentic/ files, root-level config, specifications, expertise files"
  code_access: "If code-level insight is needed, ask library-developer or library-validator to report — never read source directly."
  enforced: "2026-05-10 — user explicitly removed CTO read permissions on packages/library/"

delegation_workflow:
  mandatory_sequence: |
    After every library-developer delegation that makes code changes, you MUST delegate to library-validator for validation.
    Sequence: library-developer (implement) → library-validator (validate).
    Never skip the quality validation step. This ensures code is clean, tested, and documented.
  timeout_constraint: |
    Bash tool has a 10-minute (600000ms) timeout. Large phases must be split into sub-delegations of ~5-8 minutes each.
    Split strategy for Phase 3: (A) auth.ts + errors.ts, (B) user methods in tracker.ts, (C) auth integration into existing methods + CLI commands, (D) library-validator validation).
    Each sub-task should be scoped to a few files to stay within timeout.
  docs_ownership: |
    library-releaser owns documentation tasks: TypeDoc configuration, doc generation, docs scripts.
    When docs need updating or generating for a release, delegate to library-releaser.
    library-validator no longer handles documentation — only testing and quality gates.
  api_change_policy: |
    MANDATORY: Any change to CLI command behavior or to the API of public functions must be
    delegated to library-releaser for running the build and updating documentation.
    This applies to ALL code changes that touch public-facing surface area — whether new features,
    behavioral changes, or signature modifications. library-releaser must rebuild dist/ and update
    docs/markdown/ to reflect the change before the work is considered complete.
    ENFORCEMENT: Every /issue chain that touches CLI or public API MUST include a library-releaser
    task as part of the issue chain. Do NOT mark the parent as done until library-releaser completes.
    Violation caught in session 68: configurable-branch shipped without docs+build task.
  docs_awareness: |
    All agents have read access to docs/markdown/ (8 files: overview, getting-started, authentication,
    issue-object, hierarchy-and-blockages, storing-issues-in-git, cli-reference, javascript-reference).
    Agents can consult these docs for API details, CLI usage patterns, and feature behavior.
    library-releaser has docs_structure in its expertise file with full file listing.
    When delegating tasks, mention docs/ availability if the agent might benefit from reference material.
  access_gaps: |
    Resolved: user granted CTO access to .github/ folder. CTO now owns workflow files.
    Root .gitignore is also writable by CTO.
  validation_rejection_flow: |
    When a validator rejects an implementation (reports issues):
    1. Validator posts a comment on their issue with findings and keeps it in their status (or reopens)
    2. CTO reviews the findings and reopens the implementation issue (move back to todo/in-progress)
    3. Developer picks up the reopened issue, makes fixes, marks done again
    4. Validator re-validates — cycle continues until implementation passes
    This is the same pattern used for library issues (e.g., configurable branch mpfn4dkotn fix cycle).
  webapp_delegation_pattern: |
    Webapp issues follow sequential phases: impl → validate → next phase impl.
    ALL issues in a chain should be set to todo upfront. Blockages control the execution order.
    Only todo issues are picked up by `agt next`. Idea is invisible to the runner.
    Do NOT use idea status for work that should flow through the agent runner automatically.
  webapp_styler_pattern: |
    webapp-styler is a UI/UX specialist — does NOT write backend code or tests.
    Workflow: (1) webapp-styler audits UI and posts findings comment, (2) CTO reviews findings
    and creates implementation issues, (3) webapp-styler implements changes within scope.
    webapp-styler's domain: CSS, component styling, layout, accessibility, responsive design,
    interaction patterns, visual consistency, micro-interactions.
    webapp-styler does NOT own: backend API, data model, business logic, test infrastructure.
  note: "Self-check and validation steps are enforced via agent system prompts. No need to duplicate in delegation messages."
  library-developer:
    focus: "Focus delegation messages on the implementation task itself. The agent self-checks typecheck+lint+test before completion."
  library-validator:
    focus: "Always pass the same spec file used for implementation so quality can validate alignment with specs, not just code quality. Include the spec path, what changed, and what behaviors to validate. Handles testing and quality gates only (documentation moved to library-releaser)."
  library-releaser:
    focus: "Delegate release tasks: verify quality gates pass, generate documentation (HTML + Markdown), build artifacts, bump version, publish to npm. Provide version bump guidance (patch/minor/major) based on changes since last release. The agent owns the full release lifecycle end-to-end. Docs output: docs/html/ (users) + docs/md/ (agents) at repo root. Agent has docs/** access for writing generated documentation."

  - docs/hierarchy.md — parent-child tree, childrenOf map, status constraints, auto-promotion
  - docs/commands.md — full CLI reference: init, create, update, list, view, history, comments, blockages
  - docs/issue-blockages.md — dependency index, blockage lifecycle, cycle detection, impact scoring
  - docs/user-auth.md — token-based auth, user registry, auth modes (open/read-only/strict)

  cto_scope: ".agentic/ files, root-level config, specifications, expertise files"

delegation_workflow:
  mandatory_sequence: |
    After every library-developer delegation that makes code changes, you MUST delegate to library-validator for validation.
    Sequence: library-developer (implement) → library-validator (validate).
    Never skip the quality validation step. This ensures code is clean, tested, and documented.
  timeout_constraint: |
    Bash tool has a 10-minute (600000ms) timeout. Large phases must be split into sub-delegations of ~5-8 minutes each.
    Split strategy for Phase 3: (A) auth.ts + errors.ts, (B) user methods in tracker.ts, (C) auth integration into existing methods + CLI commands, (D) library-validator validation).
    Each sub-task should be scoped to a few files to stay within timeout.
  docs_ownership: |
    library-releaser owns documentation tasks: TypeDoc configuration, doc generation, docs scripts.
    When docs need updating or generating for a release, delegate to library-releaser.
    library-validator no longer handles documentation — only testing and quality gates.
  api_change_policy: |
    MANDATORY: Any change to CLI command behavior or to the API of public functions must be
    delegated to library-releaser for running the build and updating documentation.
    This applies to ALL code changes that touch public-facing surface area — whether new features,
    behavioral changes, or signature modifications. library-releaser must rebuild dist/ and update
    docs/markdown/ to reflect the change before the work is considered complete.
    ENFORCEMENT: Every /issue chain that touches CLI or public API MUST include a library-releaser
    task as part of the issue chain. Do NOT mark the parent as done until library-releaser completes.
    Violation caught in session 68: configurable-branch shipped without docs+build task.
  docs_awareness: |
    All agents have read access to docs/markdown/ (8 files: overview, getting-started, authentication,
    issue-object, hierarchy-and-blockages, storing-issues-in-git, cli-reference, javascript-reference).
    Agents can consult these docs for API details, CLI usage patterns, and feature behavior.
    library-releaser has docs_structure in its expertise file with full file listing.
    When delegating tasks, mention docs/ availability if the agent might benefit from reference material.
  access_gaps: |
    Resolved: user granted CTO access to .github/ folder. CTO now owns workflow files.
    Root .gitignore is also writable by CTO.
  validation_rejection_flow: |
    When a validator rejects an implementation (reports issues):
    1. Validator posts a comment on their issue with findings and keeps it in their status (or reopens)
    2. CTO reviews the findings and reopens the implementation issue (move back to todo/in-progress)
    3. Developer picks up the reopened issue, makes fixes, marks done again
    4. Validator re-validates — cycle continues until implementation passes
    This is the same pattern used for library issues (e.g., configurable branch mpfn4dkotn fix cycle).
  webapp_delegation_pattern: |
    Webapp issues follow sequential phases: impl → validate → next phase impl.
    ALL issues in a chain should be set to todo upfront. Blockages control the execution order.
    Only todo issues are picked up by `agt next`. Idea is invisible to the runner.
    Do NOT use idea status for work that should flow through the agent runner automatically.
  webapp_styler_pattern: |
    webapp-styler is a UI/UX specialist — does NOT write backend code or tests.
    Workflow: (1) webapp-styler audits UI and posts findings comment, (2) CTO reviews findings
    and creates implementation issues, (3) webapp-styler implements changes within scope.
    webapp-styler's domain: CSS, component styling, layout, accessibility, responsive design,
    interaction patterns, visual consistency, micro-interactions.
    webapp-styler does NOT own: backend API, data model, business logic, test infrastructure.
  note: "Self-check and validation steps are enforced via agent system prompts. No need to duplicate in delegation messages."
  library-developer:
    focus: "Focus delegation messages on the implementation task itself. The agent self-checks typecheck+lint+test before completion."
  library-validator:
    focus: "Always pass the same spec file used for implementation so quality can validate alignment with specs, not just code quality. Include the spec path, what changed, and what behaviors to validate. Handles testing and quality gates only (documentation moved to library-releaser)."
  library-releaser:
    focus: "Delegate release tasks: verify quality gates pass, generate documentation (HTML + Markdown), build artifacts, bump version, publish to npm. Provide version bump guidance (patch/minor/major) based on changes since last release. The agent owns the full release lifecycle end-to-end. Docs output: docs/html/ (users) + docs/md/ (agents) at repo root. Agent has docs/** access for writing generated documentation."

      description: "Store .agentrack/ on orphan branch _agentrack via git worktree. Branch-independent issue access. Two init scenarios (fresh/join). Three commands: agt init (worktree setup), agt push (auto-commit + sync), agt pull (sync from remote). New module src/worktree.ts + 2 new CLI commands. Status: IMPLEMENTED with 3 spec deviations found in validation. Fix phase: mpd4hktoxq (fix deviations) → mpd4hs14zp (validate + tests) → mpd4i06wz6 (document + build). Parent: mpcwcufhzk."
      naming_conventions: "Branch = `_agentrack`, directory = `.agentrack`, tool = `agentrack`, data inside branch = `issues/`"
    - path: docs-generation.md
      description: "SUPERSEDED by user-docs-spec.md. TypeDoc dual-format docs are being removed. Release workflow and .gitignore updated by CTO (mpdpvfn3yb done). Typedoc tooling cleanup pending (mpdpu00ksc)."

      description: "User-friendly documentation overhaul. Replace TypeDoc auto-generated docs with hand-written markdown in docs/markdown/. 8 sections: overview, getting started, authentication, issue object, hierarchy & blockages, storing in git, CLI reference, JS reference. Removes typedoc tooling entirely. Parent: mpdpt4rego. CTO config (mpdpvfn3yb) done. TypeDoc deps removed from package.json. Doc writing: mpdwq7dvls (library-releaser, replaces failed mpdpuhd0r5)."
    - path: configurable-branch-spec.md
      description: "Configurable branch name for agt init. --branch <name> flag allows custom orphan branch per agentrack instance. Normalization: strip leading _, prepend _ for branch, . for dir. Pointer file (.agentrack.json) at repo root solves circular discovery. Slash rejection (AC8). resolution.ts and tracker.ts dynamic discovery via pointer file. New module: src/core/pointer.ts (actually implemented as branch-config.ts). Enables multiple instances per repo and test isolation.     - path: e2e-validation-suite-spec.md
      description: "E2E test suite in validation/ folder. Uses real git repos + agt CLI invocations (spawn + capture). Covers all CLI commands with happy/error/edge cases. Full lifecycle test. No library code changes. Parent: mpebmstgs9. Implementation: mpebnnq5qq (library-validator)."
    - path: e2e-refactor.md
      description: "Refactor E2E tests from per-test git repos to shared worktree approach. Two test types: Type A (git ops: init/push/pull, clean git env per test) and Type B (CRUD etc., fast data reset per test). New helpers: initE2EWorktree, teardownE2EWorktree, resetWorktreeData, setAuthMode. Remove old helpers: createTestRepo, cleanupTestRepo, createIsolatedDir. Parent: mpfobnq8ty (child of mpebmstgs9).       description: "Full-stack webapp specification for agentrack UI. React 19 + Vite + shadcn/ui frontend (SPA with list and detail views), Hono + Bun backend (REST API with 21 endpoints), TanStack Query state management.   rule: "CTO must NOT read or modify files under packages/library/. All code changes go through subordinates."

delegation_workflow:
  mandatory_sequence: |
    After every library-developer delegation that makes code changes, you MUST delegate to library-validator for validation.
    Sequence: library-developer (implement) → library-validator (validate).
    Never skip the quality validation step. This ensures code is clean, tested, and documented.
  timeout_constraint: |
    Bash tool has a 10-minute (600000ms) timeout. Large phases must be split into sub-delegations of ~5-8 minutes each.
    Split strategy for Phase 3: (A) auth.ts + errors.ts, (B) user methods in tracker.ts, (C) auth integration into existing methods + CLI commands, (D) library-validator validation).
    Each sub-task should be scoped to a few files to stay within timeout.
  docs_ownership: |
    library-releaser owns documentation tasks: TypeDoc configuration, doc generation, docs scripts.
    When docs need updating or generating for a release, delegate to library-releaser.
    library-validator no longer handles documentation — only testing and quality gates.
  api_change_policy: |
    MANDATORY: Any change to CLI command behavior or to the API of public functions must be
    delegated to library-releaser for running the build and updating documentation.
    This applies to ALL code changes that touch public-facing surface area — whether new features,
    behavioral changes, or signature modifications. library-releaser must rebuild dist/ and update
    docs/markdown/ to reflect the change before the work is considered complete.
    ENFORCEMENT: Every /issue chain that touches CLI or public API MUST include a library-releaser
    task as part of the issue chain. Do NOT mark the parent as done until library-releaser completes.
    Violation caught in session 68: configurable-branch shipped without docs+build task.
  docs_awareness: |
    All agents have read access to docs/markdown/ (8 files: overview, getting-started, authentication,
    issue-object, hierarchy-and-blockages, storing-issues-in-git, cli-reference, javascript-reference).
    Agents can consult these docs for API details, CLI usage patterns, and feature behavior.
    library-releaser has docs_structure in its expertise file with full file listing.
    When delegating tasks, mention docs/ availability if the agent might benefit from reference material.
  access_gaps: |
    Resolved: user granted CTO access to .github/ folder. CTO now owns workflow files.
    Root .gitignore is also writable by CTO.
  validation_rejection_flow: |
    When a validator rejects an implementation (reports issues):
    1. Validator posts a comment on their issue with findings and keeps it in their status (or reopens)
    2. CTO reviews the findings and reopens the implementation issue (move back to todo/in-progress)
    3. Developer picks up the reopened issue, makes fixes, marks done again
    4. Validator re-validates — cycle continues until implementation passes
    This is the same pattern used for library issues (e.g., configurable branch mpfn4dkotn fix cycle).
  webapp_delegation_pattern: |
    Webapp issues follow sequential phases: impl → validate → next phase impl.
    ALL issues in a chain should be set to todo upfront. Blockages control the execution order.
    Only todo issues are picked up by `agt next`. Idea is invisible to the runner.
    Do NOT use idea status for work that should flow through the agent runner automatically.
  webapp_styler_pattern: |
    webapp-styler is a UI/UX specialist — does NOT write backend code or tests.
    Workflow: (1) webapp-styler audits UI and posts findings comment, (2) CTO reviews findings
    and creates implementation issues, (3) webapp-styler implements changes within scope.
    webapp-styler's domain: CSS, component styling, layout, accessibility, responsive design,
    interaction patterns, visual consistency, micro-interactions.
    webapp-styler does NOT own: backend API, data model, business logic, test infrastructure.
  note: "Self-check and validation steps are enforced via agent system prompts. No need to duplicate in delegation messages."
  library-developer:
    focus: "Focus delegation messages on the implementation task itself. The agent self-checks typecheck+lint+test before completion."
  library-validator:
    focus: "Always pass the same spec file used for implementation so quality can validate alignment with specs, not just code quality. Include the spec path, what changed, and what behaviors to validate. Handles testing and quality gates only (documentation moved to library-releaser)."
  library-releaser:
    focus: "Delegate release tasks: verify quality gates pass, generate documentation (HTML + Markdown), build artifacts, bump version, publish to npm. Provide version bump guidance (patch/minor/major) based on changes since last release. The agent owns the full release lifecycle end-to-end. Docs output: docs/html/ (users) + docs/md/ (agents) at repo root. Agent has docs/** access for writing generated documentation."

agt create "Webapp: Improve form UX, validation, and accessibility" \
  --description "## Context
Forms are the primary interaction mechanism (creating issues, adding comments, editing metadata). Currently they lack proper labeling, validation feedback, and accessible patterns.

## Scope

### 1. CreateIssueDialog.tsx — Form Improvements
- Add visible labels to all fields (title, description, priority, status, assignee, tags)
- Mark required fields (title) with visual indicator and \`aria-required=\"true\"\`
- Add inline validation:
  - Title: required, min length feedback
  - Description: optional hint text
- Error messages should appear below the field in red with \`role=\"alert\"\`
- Fix field spacing for visual consistency
- Focus management: auto-focus title field when dialog opens

### 2. IssueFilters.tsx — Accessibility
- Add proper labels to search input (\`aria-label=\"Search issues\"\` or visible label)
- Add \`aria-label\` to all select dropdowns
- Ensure keyboard navigation works (Tab through filters, Enter to apply)
- Add clear \"Clear filters\" action that's keyboard accessible

### 3. Issue Detail Forms
- CommentsSection.tsx: Add label to comment textarea, validation for empty submit
- TagInput.tsx: Add label, keyboard navigation for tag suggestions
- ParentSelector.tsx: Add label, accessible search/filter

### 4. General Form Patterns
- Consistent field spacing using design token spacing values
- Consistent error state styling (red border, error text below)
- Consistent button placement (primary right-aligned, secondary left)
- \`aria-describedby\` for fields with help text

## Files to Modify
- \`packages/webapp/frontend/src/components/issues/CreateIssueDialog.tsx\`
- \`packages/webapp/frontend/src/components/issues/IssueFilters.tsx\`
- \`packages/webapp/frontend/src/components/issue-detail/CommentsSection.tsx\`
- \`packages/webapp/frontend/src/components/issue-detail/TagInput.tsx\`
- \`packages/webapp/frontend/src/components/issue-detail/ParentSelector.tsx\`

- [ ] All form fields have visible labels and proper \`aria-label\` or \`<label>\` associations
- [ ] Required fields are clearly marked
- [ ] Inline validation shows errors below fields in real-time
- [ ] CreateIssueDialog auto-focuses the title field on open
- [ ] All forms are fully keyboard-navigable
- [ ] Error messages use \`role=\"alert\"\` for screen readers
- [ ] Consistent field spacing and error styling across all forms

## Constraints

The webapp layout and navigation need better visual hierarchy, responsive behavior, and information architecture. Users need clear wayfinding especially in detail views.

### 1. Header.tsx - Navigation Improvements
- Add clear visual hierarchy to navigation items
- Active page indicator (highlight current nav item)
- Improve spacing and alignment using design tokens
- Add hover states to navigation links
- Ensure navigation works on mobile (hamburger menu or sheet-based nav if not already)

### 2. AppLayout.tsx - Page Structure
- Add consistent page title region at the top of each page
- Add breadcrumb navigation in detail views (e.g., Issues > Issue #123)
- Ensure consistent content width and max-width
- Proper padding using design token spacing values
- Consider a sidebar for navigation on desktop if it improves the layout

### 3. IssueDetailPage.tsx - Detail View Layout
- Add page title showing issue title prominently
- Add breadcrumb: Issues link > Issue title
- Improve section hierarchy (details, comments, blockages, sub-issues)
- Add clear visual separation between sections
- Make the layout work on smaller screens (stack columns)

### 4. Responsive Behavior
- Test and fix layouts at breakpoints: mobile (640px), tablet (768px), desktop (1024px+)
- Issue list: stack columns on mobile
- Issue detail: single column on mobile, multi-column on desktop
- Forms: full-width on mobile, constrained on desktop
- Navigation: collapsible on mobile

- packages/webapp/frontend/src/pages/IssueDetailPage.tsx

- Header has clear active state for current page
- Detail views show breadcrumb navigation
- Page titles are prominent and consistent
- All pages render correctly at 640px, 768px, and 1024px+ widths
- No horizontal overflow on mobile
- Navigation is fully keyboard accessible
- Content has consistent padding and max-width

## Constraints
- Use design tokens for spacing, typography, colors
- Keep existing page functionality and routes intact
- Use shadcn/ui Sheet component for mobile nav if needed (already available)
